| # CANopen safety - SRDO and GFC {#canopen-safety---srdo-and-gfc-1 .p_Heading1 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

## CiA-304 implementation in RC40 BSW CANopen library: {#cia-304-implementation-in-rc40-bsw-canopen-library .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

CANopen library implements below functionality of CiA-304:

 

1.[SRDO](safety-relevant-data-object(srdo).html){.topiclink} related objects:

i.SRDO communication parameter object

ii.SRDO mapping parameter object

iii.SRDO configuration valid and checksum object

2\.  SRDO mapping table.

3\.  SRDO transmission at every refresh time.

4\.  SRDO data validation for correct order and inform ASW in case of a problem.

5\.  SRDO timeout monitoring like SCT and SRVT and inform ASW in case of a problem.

6\.  Copy of Objects from/to when send/receive.

7\.  SRDO configuration validation using the checksum and configuration valid object.

8\.  GFC producer and consumer.

The ASW shall maintain the updated data in objects mapped to SRDO and take the necessary actions based on the SRDO validation status (data incorrect/timeout). ASW can send a GFC and has to handle a GFC received.

 

## SRDO {#srdo .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Once the configuration is done by the ASW, the CANopen library handles everything needed for transmission and reception of SRDO (similar to PDO)

## For transmission: {#for-transmission .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

- If refresh time is configured, then the CANopen library will automatically start transmitting SRDO\'s in the configured interval.

- If ASW needs to trigger SRDO additional to refresh cycle then it can be done by calling bds_canopen_sendSrdo.

- The CANopen lib will fetch the data from objects based on mapping configurations and dump it into the SRDO frame (both normal and inverted telegram) in all cases.

- The ASW is only responsible for updating data in its objects which will be used by the CANopen library to transmit over SRDO.

## For Reception: {#for-reception .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

- The CANopen library will process received SRDO and automatically update the objects with values received over SRDO.

- All necessary timing monitoring requirements as per CiA-304 are handled in the CANopen library.

- ASW can get an indication upon SRDO reception by registering a callback using API bds_canopen_regSrdoRcvIndcn

- The CANopen library automatically copies SRDO data into objects. When ASW needs the value of objects over SRDO, then it can directly access its object data

 

## Global Fail safe command(GFC) {#global-fail-safe-commandgfc .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

ASW can send GFC signal using API  bds_canopen_sendGfcand for indication when a GFC is received, the callback should be registered using API  bds_canopen_regGfcRcvIndcn

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ![Info](info.png){style="margin:0;width:2.1667in;height:0.6979in;border:none"}   ASW is responsible for implementing a safety reaction. The CANopen library will only provide an indication in case of an SRDO or GFC safety event.
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

## Default configurations of SRDO {#default-configurations-of-srdo .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

 

By default in CANopen library object dictionary, SRDO configurations is set to initialized state. i.e

1.In SRDO Parameter 0x1301 to 0x1340, SubIndex 1 - Information direction is set to 0 (Uninitialized)

2.SRDO mapping parameter 0x1381 to 0x13C0, mapping parameters are set to 0 (invalid mapping)

3.Safety configuration CRC 0x13FF , SRDO related subindex is 0

4.Configuration valid 0x13FE is 0 which is SRDO configuration is not valid

 

The device will not go to an \"operational\" state with the configuration above because according to CiA-304, a minimum of one SRDO configuration should be valid.

The ASW must set default values for these SRDO parameters of its own object dictionary. This can be done by using SDO local write API  bds_canopen_sdoWriteLocal and using API  bds_canopen_calcSrdoCnfCRC checksum for configurations can be calculated. The below example demonstrates how ASW can set the SRDO objects with default values.

## SRDO CRC calculation: {#srdo-crc-calculation .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Below table explains the byte order for CRC calculations.

 

+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
| Object      | SubIndex        | Name                                     | Size            | Data            |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
| 1301h       | SRDO Communication Parameter                                                                   |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 01h             | Direction of information                 | 1 byte          | a1              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 02h             | Refresh time                             | 2 byte          | a2              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 03h             | Tx: reserved                             | 1 byte          | a3              |
|             |                 |                                          |                 |                 |
|             |                 | Rx: SRVT                                 |                 |                 |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 05h             | COB-ID 1                                 | 4 byte          | a4              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 06h             | COB-ID 2                                 | 4 byte          | a5              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
| 1381        | SRDO Mapping Parameter                                                                         |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 00h             | Highest Sub-Index Supported              | 1 byte          | b1              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 01h             | Sub-Index                                | 1 byte          | b2              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 01h             | Mapped Object 1 Index,Sub-Index and Size | 4 byte          | b3              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 02h             | Sub-Index                                | 1 byte          | b4              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 02h             | Mapped Object 2 Index,Sub-Index and Size | 4 byte          | b5              |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | .                                                                                              |
|             |                                                                                                |
|             | .                                                                                              |
|             |                                                                                                |
|             | .                                                                                              |
|             |                                                                                                |
|             | .                                                                                              |
|             |                                                                                                |
|             | .                                                                                              |
+-------------+                                                                                                |
|             |                                                                                                |
+-------------+                                                                                                |
|             |                                                                                                |
+-------------+                                                                                                |
|             |                                                                                                |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 0Fh             | Sub-Index                                | 1 byte          | b30             |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 0Fh             | Mapped Object 3 Index,Sub-Index and Size | 4 byte          | b31             |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 10h             | Sub-Index                                | 4 byte          | b32             |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
|             | 10h             | Mapped Object 4 Index,Sub-Index and Size | 4 byte          | b33             |
|             |                 |                                          |                 |                 |
|             |                 |                                          |                 |                 |
|             |                 |                                          |                 |                 |
|             |                 |                                          |                 |                 |
+-------------+-----------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+

 

The generator polynomial shall be: G(x) = x16+x12+x5+1

The following databytes are used to calculate check-sum: a1,a2,a3,a4,a5,b1,b2,b3,b4,b5\...\...b30,b31,b32,b33
